question_text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Umami is one of the five basic tastes, along with sweet, sour, salty, and bitter.
• Umami is the savory taste that the tongue detects when it senses glutamate, an amino acid.
• Foods that are rich in glutamate include aged cheese, ripe tomatoes, and mushrooms.
• The Japanese chemist Kikunae Ikeda identified umami as a distinct taste in 1908.
• Ikeda isolated glutamate from kombu, a type of edible seaweed.

The student wants to define the term "umami" for a general audience that is unfamiliar with it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
answer_a: Umami, one of the five basic tastes, is the savory flavor that the tongue detects when it senses glutamate, an amino acid found in foods such as aged cheese and mushrooms.
answer_b: Umami is the savory taste produced when the tongue detects glutamate, and it is the strongest and most important of the five basic tastes, found in aged cheese, ripe tomatoes, and mushrooms.
answer_c: In 1908, the Japanese chemist Kikunae Ikeda identified umami as a distinct taste when he isolated glutamate, an amino acid, from kombu, a type of edible seaweed.
answer_d: Umami is one of the five basic tastes, along with sweet, sour, salty, and bitter, and it is the taste that the tongue detects in aged cheese, ripe tomatoes, and mushrooms.
explanation: Choice A is the best answer because it accomplishes the stated goal of defining "umami" for readers who are new to the term. It says what umami is (one of the five basic tastes), describes how it tastes (savory), and explains what causes it (the tongue detecting glutamate, an amino acid), and it adds familiar foods that contain glutamate to make the idea concrete. All of this information comes directly from the notes.
distractor_b_explanation: Choice B is incorrect. Although it does mention the savory taste and glutamate, it overclaims by calling umami "the strongest and most important" of the basic tastes, which the notes never state.
distractor_c_explanation: Choice C is incorrect. This choice describes the history of the discovery of umami (who identified it, when, and from what source) rather than explaining what umami is. A reader unfamiliar with the term would still not know what umami tastes like or what causes it.
distractor_d_explanation: Choice D is incorrect. This choice places umami among the five basic tastes and names foods in which it is found, but it never says what umami is: it omits the savory quality and the role of glutamate. A reader new to the term would still not understand the concept, because the sentence lists examples without defining it.

question_text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Architects compared two floor systems for a six-story office building: cross-laminated timber (CLT) panels and reinforced concrete slabs.
• The CLT system weighed about 100 kilograms per square meter of floor.
• The reinforced concrete system weighed about 500 kilograms per square meter of floor.
• Crews installed the CLT panels in about 3 days per level, whereas the concrete floors needed about 14 days per level to cure.
• The CLT panels cost about 12 percent more per square meter than the concrete slabs.
• Both floor systems earned the same 90-minute fire-resistance rating.

The student wants to contrast the weight of the two floor systems using specific figures. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
answer_a: Crews installed the CLT panels in about 3 days per level, while the concrete floors needed about 14 days per level to cure before work above could continue.
answer_b: Per square meter of floor, the CLT system was much lighter than the reinforced concrete system, and both systems earned the same 90-minute fire rating.
answer_c: Per square meter of floor, the CLT system weighed about 500 kilograms, whereas the reinforced concrete system weighed only about 100 kilograms.
answer_d: Per square meter of floor, the CLT system weighed about 100 kilograms, whereas the reinforced concrete system weighed about 500 kilograms.
explanation: Choice D is the best answer because it contrasts the two systems on the specified dimension, weight, and uses both figures from the notes accurately. It states that the CLT system weighed about 100 kilograms per square meter and that the reinforced concrete system weighed about 500 kilograms per square meter, which allows a reader to see that the concrete system was five times as heavy.
distractor_a_explanation: Choice A is incorrect because it contrasts the systems on installation time (3 days versus 14 days per level), not weight. The information is accurate but does not accomplish the stated goal.
distractor_b_explanation: Choice B is incorrect because it describes the weight difference only loosely ("much lighter") without the specific figures the goal requires, and it adds the fire-rating note, which is irrelevant to a weight contrast.
distractor_c_explanation: Choice C is incorrect because it reverses the figures from the notes, attributing about 500 kilograms to the CLT system and about 100 kilograms to the reinforced concrete system. This inverts the actual contrast.

question_text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• A sea breeze is a wind that blows from the ocean toward the land along a coastline.
• On sunny days, land heats up faster than ocean water does.
• Air above the warm land becomes warmer and less dense than the air above the ocean, so it rises.
• Cooler, denser air from over the ocean moves inland to replace the rising air.
• Sea breezes usually begin in late morning and peak in mid-afternoon.
• Coastal cities with sea breezes often have afternoon temperatures several degrees lower than nearby inland towns.

The student wants to explain to a group of middle-school students why a sea breeze forms on sunny days. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
answer_a: Sea breezes usually begin in late morning and peak in mid-afternoon, often leaving coastal cities several degrees cooler than nearby inland towns during the hottest part of the day.
answer_b: On sunny days, land heats up faster than the ocean, so the air above the land rises and cooler air from over the water moves inland to replace it, forming a sea breeze.
answer_c: Because land heats up faster than ocean water on sunny days, the air above the land becomes warmer and less dense than the air above the nearby ocean surface.
answer_d: Cool ocean water pushes air toward the shore, which is why coastal cities often have afternoon temperatures several degrees lower than nearby inland towns.
explanation: Choice B is the best answer because it explains the cause-and-effect chain for a young audience in plain language. The notes state that land heats faster than the ocean on sunny days, that the air above the land rises, and that cooler ocean air moves inland to replace it. Choice B links these steps in cause-and-effect order and names the result, a sea breeze, which is exactly what the student wants to explain.
distractor_a_explanation: Choice A is incorrect. It gives only effects of sea breezes, namely when they occur and how they cool coastal cities. These details are accurate, but they do not explain why a sea breeze forms.
distractor_c_explanation: Choice C is incorrect. It gives only the first part of the cause, that the air above warm land becomes less dense. It never connects this to cooler ocean air moving inland, so it does not explain how a sea breeze results.
distractor_d_explanation: Choice D is incorrect. It makes an unsupported causal claim. The notes attribute sea breezes to rising air over warm land and cooler air replacing it, not to ocean water pushing air toward the shore.

question_text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Pottery that has been shaped from wet clay and left to dry is called greenware.
• Greenware is fragile and can dissolve back into slush if it is soaked in water.
• Greenware is fired in a kiln to about 1,000°C in a first firing called the bisque firing.
• After the bisque firing, the piece is called bisqueware, which is hard, porous, and no longer dissolves in water.
• A second, hotter firing at about 1,250°C melts the glaze that was applied to the bisqueware into a glassy, waterproof coating.
• Many studios use electric kilns with digital controllers that raise the temperature automatically.

The student wants to explain to beginners how a piece of pottery changes before and after the bisque firing. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
answer_a: During the bisque firing, an electric kiln with a digital controller automatically raises the temperature to about 1,000°C to harden the greenware.
answer_b: Hard, porous bisqueware that no longer dissolves in water turns into fragile greenware that can dissolve into slush once the bisque firing is complete.
answer_c: Fragile greenware that can dissolve back into slush in water becomes hard, porous bisqueware that no longer dissolves once it has gone through the bisque firing.
answer_d: Greenware is glazed and fired once at about 1,250°C, which hardens the clay and also melts the glaze into a glassy, waterproof coating.
explanation: Choice C is the best answer because it describes both stages the student wants to explain for beginners: before the bisque firing, the piece is fragile greenware that can dissolve into slush in water, and after the firing it is hard, porous bisqueware that no longer dissolves. The sentence presents the stages in the correct order and uses only information from the notes.
distractor_a_explanation: Choice A is incorrect. It focuses on the equipment (the electric kiln and its digital controller) and the firing temperature, which is trivia about the process, and it never contrasts the piece before and after the firing, so it does not accomplish the student's goal.
distractor_b_explanation: Choice B is incorrect. It reverses the order of the stages, claiming that bisqueware turns into greenware. According to the notes, the bisque firing changes greenware into bisqueware, not the other way around.
distractor_d_explanation: Choice D is incorrect. It merges two separate firings into one, combining the glaze and the 1,250°C second firing with the hardening of the clay. The notes say the clay is hardened in the first (bisque) firing at about 1,000°C and glazed afterward, so this choice misrepresents the process and does not clearly show the before and after of the bisque firing.

question_text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• African elephants and Asian elephants are both herbivores that spend most of the day foraging for plant matter.
• Both species live in herds that are led by an older female, usually the oldest in the group.
• African elephants have ears that can span more than a meter across.
• Asian elephants have ears that are noticeably smaller than those of African elephants.
• Both male and female African elephants grow tusks, but among Asian elephants only some males grow prominent tusks.
• African elephants live in the savannas and forests of sub-Saharan Africa, while Asian elephants live in the forests and grasslands of South and Southeast Asia.

The student wants to state one way African and Asian elephants are alike and one way their physical features differ. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
answer_a: Both African elephants and Asian elephants are herbivores that spend most of the day foraging, and both species live in herds that are led by an older female.
answer_b: Although African elephants have ears that can span more than a meter and Asian elephants have noticeably smaller ears, both species live in herds led by an older female.
answer_c: Unlike Asian elephants, among which only some males grow prominent tusks, African elephants of both sexes grow tusks, and the two species live in different regions.
answer_d: Both species live in herds led by an older female, but it is Asian elephants, rather than African elephants, that have ears spanning more than a meter across.
explanation: Choice B is the best answer because it states both a similarity and a difference in physical features, as the student's goal requires. The sentence contrasts the ear size of African elephants (ears that can span more than a meter) with that of Asian elephants (noticeably smaller ears), and it notes that both species live in herds led by an older female, which the notes support.
distractor_a_explanation: Choice A is incorrect. It gives two similarities, that both species are herbivores and live in herds led by an older female, but it gives no difference in physical features between the species.
distractor_c_explanation: Choice C is incorrect. It describes a physical difference (tusks) and a difference in range, but it gives no similarity between African and Asian elephants.
distractor_d_explanation: Choice D is incorrect. It correctly gives the similarity about herds, but it assigns the large ears to the wrong species; the notes say it is African elephants whose ears can span more than a meter.
